core_obligations: Perfect case (proof lines 2978-3004): omega gives a g^{g-1}_{2g-2}, thinned to a g^1_{2g-2} and realized as phi : X -> P^1_k of degree d <= 2g - 2, finite locally free; picking a rational t and any x over it gives [kappa(x) : k] <= d, and over a perfect field every residue field is separable.
Reduction (proof lines 3005-3008): only an infinite field of characteristic p > 0 remains.

Infinite char p case (proof lines 3010-3030): X^{(p)} has the same positive genus, so by the grd inequalities it has no g^{g-1}_d with d <= g - 1; applying the inseparable-linear-system lemma to the canonical series excludes possibility (2) since 2g - 2 over p is at most g - 1, yielding phi of degree <= 2g - 2 that is generically etale.

Closing (proof lines 3020-3030): the etale locus U maps to a nonempty open of P^1_k containing a k-rational point t (k infinite); any u over t has kappa(u)/kappa(t) separable, kappa(t) = k, and degree <= 2g - 2.
proof_roadmap: Build the canonical g^{g-1}_{2g-2} from omega and thin it to a pencil giving phi : X -> P^1 of degree <= 2g - 2.
In the perfect case finish by degree bookkeeping over a rational target point.
In infinite characteristic p use the Frobenius twist: grd inequalities on X^{(p)} plus the inseparable dichotomy force a generically etale pencil.
Pick a rational point inside the image of the etale locus and read off the separable bound.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a low-degree separable closed point on any smooth proper curve of genus >= 2 (statement lines 2971-2976). The proof (lines 2978-3030) splits into the perfect case (pencil from the canonical series, finite locally free degree bookkeeping) and the infinite characteristic-p case (Frobenius twist X^{(p)}, grd inequalities excluding small-degree series on the twist, the inseparable-linear-system dichotomy excluding possibility (2), then separability harvested over the etale locus at a rational point). Every step is present with no omissions. H3: the two-case structure with the Frobenius twist argument is a genuine research-level maneuver.
